page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head across the top, with the page number "62" at the top left. No margin notes. Below the text, the catchword "dunt" at the right.

main_text.l: eorum sæuitia: attamen, quantum in ipsis est,
& condemnant, & ignis fornaces aperiunt.
Item. Sunt quidam sic addicti suis opinioni-
bus, ut, quantum in ipsis est, ex die noctem fa-
ciant: & quia in absurda imaginatione occaluerunt,
non credunt alios recte sapere, his tam
iniqui ut malint mendacibus obtrectationi-
bus credere: ne quid dicam de his, qui propter
malam conscientiam, quod de aliis dicitur, ad
se trahunt, & quicquid de quibusdam loquaris, ad
se pertinere putant: atque inde, ut fit, nouas
confingunt fabulas & tragoedias, contenti suas
suspiciones dicere vel scribere. Item. Non
est contendendum cum eo qui dat operam, ut
quomodocunq; fiat superior, & modo victor
habeatur, veras rationes negligit. Iustinus
Martyr in Epist. ad Zenam & Serenum [?].
LXXXVII.
Philosophiam nomine habituq; profiten-
tur quidam, qui nihil præstant dignum hac professione. Iustinus
LXXXVIII.
Vereratorie [?] instructi persuadendi arte
seducunt mentes imperitorum, eosq; captiuos
ducunt, deprauantes eloquia Domini: mali e-
narratores facti eorum quæ bene dicta sunt.
Item. Verborum quidem artificio simplices eo
probabiliter adducunt, ut aliquo modo in-
quirant: sed improbabiliter ipsos perdunt,
dum aduersus summum opificem impiam red-

page.notes: Small marks in the left margin (a dot and short strokes beside the first lines) are not legible text and are left out. The reading "Vereratorie" in the second-last section is uncertain. The name in the citation after "Zenam &" is printed as "Serennm" and read here as "Serenum". The "2." after "in" in the Apologia citation is hard to make out. The running head is read as "Charact. Iesvitæ" and may be abbreviated differently. The paragraph "Item. Non est" begins mid-line and is kept inside the same paragraph as printed.
